notes: Each eval labels the cheapest (model, effort) pair the rubric should produce. `models` is the expected model; `within_one_tier` marks whether an adjacent tier also passes the lenient assertion; `effort_ok` lists acceptable effort values (null for Haiku); `forbid_models` are hard-constraint failures.

evals.name: tickets-classify
evals.prompt: ok I've got support_tickets_sept.csv (~300 rows, columns id, subject, body). label each one as billing / bug / feature / other and write labels.csv with id,label. our support lead will skim the result before we act on it
evals.expected_output: Haiku 4.5, effort null. Mechanical classification with a schema and a human skim; high volume.

evals.name: uppercase-cities
evals.prompt: convert the 80 city names in cities.txt to uppercase, one per line, and save the result as cities_upper.txt
evals.expected_output: Haiku 4.5, effort null. Trivial transform.

evals.name: extract-contacts
evals.prompt: here are 40 email signatures I pasted into signatures.txt. pull out name, email and company for each into contacts.json as a list of objects. some signatures are messy (multiple phone numbers, job titles on the same line as the name)
evals.expected_output: Haiku 4.5 (effort null) or Sonnet 5 at low. Extraction into a checkable schema, but the messiness needs minor judgment and nobody checks the output, so either tier-0 or tier-1 is defensible; anything above is over-commitment.

evals.name: dry-run-flag
evals.prompt: add a --dry-run flag to scripts/cleanup.py that prints what would be deleted without deleting anything. follow the existing argparse pattern in that file. then run pytest tests/test_cleanup.py and make sure it's green
evals.expected_output: Sonnet 5 at low or medium. Bounded single-file change with a test checker.

evals.name: revenue-script
evals.prompt: write a python script that reads orders.csv (columns order_id, date, amount, currency) and prints total revenue per month converted to USD using the rates in rates.json. keep it to one file, stdlib only
evals.expected_output: Sonnet 5 at low or medium. Small well-specified script.

evals.name: offsite-transcript-summary
evals.prompt: offsite_transcript.md is the 40-page transcript of our leadership offsite last week. give me the decisions made, who owns each one, deadlines mentioned, and a list of open questions nobody answered
evals.expected_output: Sonnet 5 at medium (high acceptable). Unverified summary with some judgment; not Haiku because nobody checks it.

evals.name: date-parse-tests
evals.prompt: write unit tests for utils/date_parse.py covering the edge cases listed in its docstring (empty string, timezone offsets, leap day, two-digit years). use pytest like the rest of tests/ and run them
evals.expected_output: Sonnet 5 at low or medium. Scoped, verifiable.

evals.name: rename-across-src
evals.prompt: rename getUserData to fetchUserProfile everywhere in src/ (about 30 files) and fix the imports and the two places it's referenced in docs/. npm test needs to stay green
evals.expected_output: Sonnet 5 at low or medium. Mechanical multi-file change with a checker.

evals.name: notifications-feature
evals.prompt: implement docs/spec-notifications.md end to end: a postgres migration for the notifications table, the service layer in src/services/notifications.ts, REST endpoints in src/api/notifications.ts, and update the React inbox component in web/src/Inbox.tsx to show unread counts. the tests in tests/ must pass when you're done
evals.expected_output: Opus 5.5 at medium (low or high acceptable; Fable acceptable). Multi-file feature, long-horizon coding, checker exists; Opus 5.5 at medium matches Opus 5 at high in fewer tokens.

evals.name: auth-pr-review
evals.prompt: review PR #482 (the diff is in pr-482.diff, about 1200 lines, it touches session handling and the password reset flow) for bugs and security issues. report everything you find, even low severity, with a confidence for each
evals.expected_output: Opus 5.5 at low or medium. Finding vulnerabilities in source code is explicitly allowed on Opus 5.5; Fable excluded by the classifier constraint; review accuracy holds at lower effort.

evals.name: grafana-screenshot
evals.prompt: attached: grafana_incident.png, our dashboard during yesterday's outage (12 panels, small text). which service caused the p99 latency spike at 14:32 and why do you think so?
evals.expected_output: Opus 5.5 at low or medium (high acceptable; Fable acceptable). Dense-image floor excludes Haiku and Sonnet; Opus 5.5 reads dense charts at low better than Opus 5 at max.

evals.name: three-statement-model
evals.prompt: build a 3-statement financial model in Excel from assumptions.md: monthly for 3 years, income statement, balance sheet and cash flow on separate sheets with linked formulas, plus a summary sheet with charts. our CFO will review it before the board meeting
evals.expected_output: Opus 5.5 at medium or high (Fable acceptable). Office deliverable with non-trivial formulas; Opus 5.5 is documented as better at financial modeling.

evals.name: contracts-long-context
evals.prompt: I've dumped all 180 vendor contracts into contracts/ (roughly 600K tokens in total). find every clause that conflicts with our new data retention policy in policy.md and list them with contract name, clause number and the conflicting sentence
evals.expected_output: Opus 5 or Fable 5.1 at medium or high. Context over 200K excludes Haiku. Opus is the documented long-context value pick; Fable is defensible only through the costly-and-unverified step-up, not through the research exception (600K input tokens at twice the rate dominate the bill).

evals.name: scheduler-deadlock
evals.prompt: our job scheduler (repo in ./scheduler) has a rare deadlock we've been chasing for weeks, maybe 1 in 500 runs. three stack dumps are in dumps/. find the root cause and fix it with a regression test that actually reproduces it
evals.expected_output: Fable 5.1 at high (xhigh acceptable; Opus at xhigh acceptable). Complexity 3 with latent-difficulty markers.

evals.name: mvp-autonomous
evals.prompt: brief.md is the product brief. build the whole MVP end to end: postgres schema, fastapi backend, react frontend, tests, and a deploy script for fly.io. ask me any clarifying questions first, then run autonomously for as long as it takes
evals.expected_output: Fable 5.1 at high (Opus acceptable). Whole-system, hours-long autonomous run, ambiguity.

evals.name: vectordb-research-memo
evals.prompt: research and compare Pinecone, Weaviate, Qdrant, Milvus, pgvector and Chroma on 12 criteria (pricing, metadata filtering, hybrid search, multi-tenancy, managed vs self-hosted, SDK maturity, ...) with sources for every claim, and write a decision memo for our platform team
evals.expected_output: Fable 5.1 at low or medium (Opus at medium acceptable). Research and synthesis: flat effort curve, Fable at low documented to win on cost per task; long deliverable so not xhigh/max.

evals.name: flaky-concurrent-test
evals.prompt: tests/test_sync.py::test_concurrent_upload fails about 1 in 20 runs on CI and always passes locally. fix it
evals.expected_output: Opus 5.5 at medium or high (Sonnet at high/xhigh or Fable acceptable). Short prompt with latent-difficulty markers: intermittent failure, passes locally.

evals.name: fuzz-harness-triage
evals.prompt: write a libFuzzer harness for our image parser (src/img/decode.c) and triage whatever crashes it finds in the first hour: dedupe by stack, rank by likely exploitability, and propose fixes
evals.expected_output: Opus 5.5 or Opus 5 at high or xhigh. Dual-use security shape: Fable excluded by the classifier constraint; Opus 5.5 may decline the triage half, Opus 5 is the documented fallback.

evals.name: skill-driven-deck
evals.prompt: use the slide-design skill to turn docs/q3-review.md into a 12-slide deck (pptx) for the leadership meeting on thursday. one message per slide, keep the numbers from the doc
evals.context: Session has the slide-design skill available. Its description: creates cognitively optimized slides and decks using five design principles; it prescribes an outline step, a build step with bundled scripts, and a render-and-check pass.
evals.expected_output: Sonnet 5 at high (Opus at medium acceptable). A skill with bundled scripts does the mechanical work; what remains is per-slide judgment. Not Haiku, not Fable (rule-heavy skill, over-commitment).

evals.name: three-connector-workflow
evals.prompt: read the unread emails in my Gmail under the Clients label, create a Trello card on the Follow-ups board for each one that asks me a question, then post a one-line summary of the new cards in Slack #client-ops
evals.context: Session has Gmail, Trello, and Slack MCP connectors available as deferred tools (the executor must load their schemas with a tool search first).
evals.expected_output: Opus 5 at medium or Sonnet 5 at high. Three connectors with writes visible to others: effort floor medium, horizon capped at 2 (plumbing), confirm-before-write instead of a bigger model. Not Haiku (multi-tool orchestration), not Fable.

evals.name: short-fix-large-repo
evals.prompt: fix the bug where the invoice total is off by exactly the tax amount on refunds
evals.context: Working directory is a monorepo of about 2,400 source files. No knowledge graph or architecture doc exists. The test suite exists but takes about 40 minutes to run.
evals.expected_output: Opus 5 at medium or high (Sonnet at high/xhigh acceptable). Two-line prompt against a large unfamiliar repo is a latent marker; refund tax logic needs reasoning; the checker is slow so no step-down.

evals.name: skill-with-scripts
evals.prompt: use the graphify skill to build the knowledge graph for ./services/billing and then tell me which modules call the payment gateway client
evals.context: Session has the graphify skill available. Its description: turns a folder of code into a persistent knowledge graph with bundled build and query scripts; building and querying are deterministic script runs.
evals.expected_output: Sonnet 5 at low or medium. The skill's scripts do the heavy lifting; the remaining work is running them and reading one query result. Opus or Fable would be over-commitment.

evals.name: session-follow-up
evals.prompt: now do the same for the other three endpoints we discussed
evals.context: This is a follow-up turn in an ongoing session; the earlier turns are not available to the grader.
evals.expected_output: Verdict is provisional; the key output is detecting the session dependency and recommending in-session execution on the session's model. Sonnet or Opus at low to high all acceptable; not Haiku, not Fable.

evals.name: multi-hour-migration
evals.prompt: migrate our 300-module python 2 code base (repo in ./legacy) to python 3 over the next few hours using parallel subagents, module by module, and keep the test suite green throughout. commit after each module
evals.context: The repo has about 300 modules and a test suite that runs in about 6 minutes. This is a mechanical migration with well-known patterns, not an unsolved problem.
evals.expected_output: Opus 5.5 at high (medium acceptable; Fable acceptable within one tier). The Opus 5.5 docs name multi-hour migrations with parallel subagents as its territory; Fable is for multiday or unsolved work.
